subject: cs0075-code-snippets

title: In the module's learning-and-prediction workflow, what does a trained model use to produce predicted data?
options: Only the labels from training data
explanation: The workflow shows new data entering the trained model during the prediction phase to produce predicted data.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Introduction to Machine Learning
title: Which activity is listed as part of preprocessing in the module's machine-learning workflow?
options: Choose the final class by argmax
explanation: The introductory workflow lists clean data and format data under preprocessing.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Feature Scaling
title: For the scaler example with original values [10, 20, 30, 40, 50], what value is produced for 30 by StandardScaler?
explanation: The scaler notes show the transformed values [-1.41, -0.71, 0.00, 0.71, 1.41].

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Feature Scaling
title: Which range is associated with MinMaxScaler in the scaler notes?
explanation: The notes state that MinMaxScaler transforms values into the range 0 to 1.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Linear Regression
title: Which regularization method can make some coefficients exactly zero, causing the model to ignore those features?
explanation: The supervised-learning notes describe Lasso as L1 regularization and state that some coefficients can become exactly zero.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Logistic Regression
title: Which outcome structure is used by binary logistic regression?
options: Two possible classes such as 0/1 or yes/no
A continuous target with no classes
explanation: The logistic-regression notes describe binary outcomes with examples such as success/failure, 0/1, and true/false.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Logistic Regression
title: What does the logistic, or sigmoid, function do to a real-valued input?
options: Maps it to a value between 0 and 1
Converts it into a word count
explanation: The notes describe the sigmoid as an S-shaped function that maps any real-valued number to a value between 0 and 1, without reaching either limit.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Logistic Regression
title: According to the threshold rule shown in the logistic-regression notes, a predicted value greater than 0.5 is assigned to which class?
explanation: The notes state that a predicted value greater than 0.5 is prediction 1; otherwise it is 0.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Logistic Regression
title: Which statement describes multinomial logistic regression in the notes?
options: It has more than two possible discrete outcomes
It can only predict yes or no
It requires the outcome categories to be ordered
explanation: The notes define multinomial logistic regression for categorical dependent variables with two or more discrete outcomes, and contrast it with the binary case.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Logistic Regression
title: Which example is ordinal rather than merely multinomial?
options: Transport type: car, train, bus, bike
School destination: college, trade school, industry
explanation: Poor, average, and good have a natural order, which is the defining feature of the ordinal setting.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Softmax / Ordinal Logistic
title: In multinomial logistic regression, what does softmax convert into class probabilities?
explanation: The softmax notes state that softmax converts the model's scores, also called logits, into class probabilities.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Softmax / Ordinal Logistic
title: For z = [2.5, 1.2, 0.3] corresponding to Setosa, Versicolor, and Virginica, which class is predicted?
options: No class because the values are logits
explanation: The notes give softmax probabilities of approximately [0.723, 0.197, 0.080], so Setosa has the largest probability.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Softmax / Ordinal Logistic
title: What do the class probabilities produced by softmax sum to?
explanation: Softmax normalizes the class scores into a probability distribution whose entries sum to 1.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Softmax / Ordinal Logistic
title: In the ordinal example, if P(Y<=3)=0.80 and P(Y<=2)=0.40, what is P(Y=3)?
explanation: The notes obtain a middle ordinal class by subtraction: P(Y=3)=P(Y<=3)-P(Y<=2)=0.80-0.40=0.40.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Softmax / Ordinal Logistic
title: Why can a displayed tie between ordinal-class probabilities disappear when full precision is used?
options: Rounded values can hide a small difference
Softmax always removes the largest class
All probabilities are rounded down to zero
explanation: The notes show values such as 0.3999998 and 0.4000001, which round to the same displayed value even though one is larger.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: Why is the Naive Bayes assumption called naive?
options: It assumes conditional independence among the input features
explanation: The Naive Bayes notes call the assumption naive because the input features are treated as conditionally independent.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: Which Naive Bayes variant is described as suitable for continuous features assumed to follow a normal distribution?
explanation: The notes describe Gaussian Naive Bayes as suitable for continuous data whose features follow a normal distribution.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: Which Naive Bayes variant is associated with discrete data where word counts matter?
explanation: The notes identify Multinomial Naive Bayes as useful for discrete data, especially text classification where word counts matter.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: Which Naive Bayes variant is designed for binary or Boolean features, such as word presence or absence?
explanation: Bernoulli Naive Bayes is described as appropriate for binary or Boolean features and for text presence/absence data.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: Which Naive Bayes variant is specifically described for categorical data with discrete, non-numeric values?
explanation: The notes describe Categorical Naive Bayes as intended for categorical data with discrete, non-numeric values.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: According to the Naive Bayes procedure in the notes, what is the first step?
options: Convert the dataset into frequency tables
Choose the class with the maximum posterior
explanation: The notes list converting the dataset into frequency tables as step 1, followed by likelihood tables and posterior calculation.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: In the notation used by the Naive Bayes notes, what is P(y)?
explanation: The notes explicitly call P(y) the class probability.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: Why can the evidence denominator be ignored when comparing Naive Bayes classes for one fixed observation?
options: It is the same for every candidate class
It is always equal to zero
It is the same as the prior probability
It is only used by GaussianNB
explanation: For a fixed observation, the evidence denominator does not depend on the candidate class, so it does not change which numerator is largest.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: In the golf example with Rainy, Hot, High, and False, which class has the larger normalized posterior?
options: The notes do not calculate it
explanation: The notes calculate P(Play=YES|X)=0.22 and P(Play=NO|X)=0.60, so the prediction is NO.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: Which is listed as an advantage of the Naive Bayes classifier?
options: It is easy to implement and fast
It always needs a very large training set
It is sensitive to every irrelevant feature
It requires the features to be ordered
explanation: The notes list being easy to implement and fast, needing less training data, and being less sensitive to irrelevant features as advantages.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Feature Scaling
title: The mean of values transformed by StandardScaler becomes approximately _____.
explanation: The scaler notes state that StandardScaler makes the mean approximately 0.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Feature Scaling
title: MinMaxScaler transforms values into a range whose upper bound is _____.
explanation: The notes state that MinMaxScaler transforms values into the range 0 to 1.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Logistic Regression
title: The S-shaped function used by binary logistic regression is the _____ function.
explanation: The logistic-regression notes identify the logistic function as the sigmoid function.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Logistic Regression
title: Logistic regression for more than two discrete outcome classes is called _____ logistic regression.
explanation: The notes use multinomial logistic regression for categorical outcomes with more than two possible outcomes.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Softmax / Ordinal Logistic
title: The unnormalized class scores supplied to softmax are called _____.
explanation: The softmax notes call the values z=[2.5,1.2,0.3] logits or scores.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Softmax / Ordinal Logistic
title: The operation used to choose the class with the highest probability is _____.
explanation: The notes select the predicted class with argmax of the class probabilities.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: Naive Bayes assumes conditional _____ among the input features.
explanation: Conditional independence among the input features is the simplifying assumption described in the notes.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: The probability P(y) is also called the _____ probability.
explanation: The notation section of the notes labels P(y) as the class probability.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: The final Naive Bayes prediction is the class with the _____ posterior probability.
explanation: The notes state that the class with the maximum posterior value is the final prediction.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: The Naive Bayes assumption treats the features as making an _____ contribution to the outcome.
explanation: The notes describe the fundamental assumption as each feature making an independent and equal contribution.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Feature Scaling
title: True or False: StandardScaler restricts every transformed value to the range 0 to 1. _____
explanation: The notes associate the 0-to-1 range with MinMaxScaler; StandardScaler does not restrict values to a fixed range.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Feature Scaling
title: True or False: MinMaxScaler is sensitive to outliers. _____
explanation: Sensitivity to outliers is listed as a MinMaxScaler characteristic in the notes.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Logistic Regression
title: True or False: Binary logistic regression is used for more than two discrete outcome classes. _____
explanation: The notes define binary logistic regression for dichotomous outcomes; more than two outcomes are described under multinomial logistic regression.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Logistic Regression
title: True or False: The sigmoid function reaches exactly 0 and exactly 1 for finite inputs. _____
explanation: The notes say the sigmoid maps into values between 0 and 1 but never exactly at those limits.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Softmax / Ordinal Logistic
title: True or False: Multinomial logistic regression uses the softmax function. _____
explanation: The softmax notes contrast binary logistic regression using sigmoid with multinomial logistic regression using softmax.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Softmax / Ordinal Logistic
title: True or False: In ordinal logistic regression, the order of the outcome categories matters. _____
explanation: The notes distinguish ordinal classes from merely different categories because their order matters.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: True or False: Naive Bayes assumes conditional independence among the input features. _____
explanation: Conditional independence is the basic assumption identified in the Naive Bayes notes.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: True or False: Gaussian Naive Bayes is the variant described for binary or Boolean features. _____
explanation: The notes associate binary or Boolean features with Bernoulli Naive Bayes and continuous normal data with Gaussian Naive Bayes.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: True or False: For one fixed observation, the Naive Bayes evidence denominator is the same for every candidate class. _____
explanation: The notes explain that the denominator does not depend on y, so it is constant while classes are compared.

subject: cs0075-code-snippets
label: Naive Bayes
title: True or False: The final Naive Bayes prediction is the class with the smallest posterior probability. _____
explanation: The notes state that the class with the maximum posterior value is selected.
